source: Olympia Infoglobe transition effects, mapped with the Protocol Explorer (web UI) on 2026-11-01

15.name: Even-odd reveal
15.text:
New characters replace the dashes in place, one at a time, in two passes.
- **Pass 1, left to right:** positions 2, 4, 6, 8 (X, then 1, then the two trailing dashes go dark).
- **Pass 2, right to left:** positions 7, 5, 3, 1 (the last dash, then 5, then the space, then F).
- Slow, with long pauses between steps.

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx15_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Confirmed: even positions left to right (5, A, C, E: “153A5C7E”), then odd positions right to left (D, B, :).

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

16.text: Okay this one drops the old text into bottom of frame liek an elevator going down, then new text comes in like an elevator going up.
16.name: Elevator up

17.text: Okay this one move the old text into top of frame liek an elevator going up, then new text comes in like an elevator going down.
17.name: Elevator down

18.text: Okay this one drops the old text into bottom of frame liek an elevator going down, then new text comes in like an elevator going dpwn.
18.name: Drop through

19.text: Okay this one drops the old text into bottom of frame liek an elevator going up, then new text comes in like an elevator going up.
19.name: Lift through

22.name: Letter shuffle
22.text:
Nothing moves; letters switch off and on in place.
- **Out:** every other dash goes dark first, then the rest disappear left to right (the rightmost one is last).
- **Blank** for about 1 s.
- **In:** letters appear one at a time in a scrambled order: X, the last 2, F, then the first 2.
- Whole transition takes about 3 s.

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_221913804.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_221913804_fx22_frames.png). Check the in-order on the globe; 8 fps sampling could hide a quick step._

23.name: Two-pass swap ↔
23.text:
Letters switch off and on in place, two passes each way, with a blank in between.
- **Out:** positions 2, 4, 6, 8 go dark left to right (“1 3 5 7” is left), then 7, 5, 3, 1 right to left.
- **In:** positions 2, 4, 6, 8 light up left to right (“3 A C E”), then 7, 5, 3, 1 right to left (D, B, :, 2).
- Slow, with a long pause between the passes. FX 22 seems to be the version where both passes go left to right.

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_fx23_frames.png)._

24.name: Bounce up
24.text:
The dashes drop out of the bottom of the band. The new text rises from the bottom **upside down**, then flips upright once it is in place (community docs: "flies up from bottom, bounces off top, mirrors once").

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx23_24_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Confirmed: old text drops away, new text rises upside down and flips upright.

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

25.name: Bounce down
25.text:
Mirror of FX 24: the dashes lift out of the top, the new text comes down from the top **upside down**, then flips upright.

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx25_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Confirmed: mirror of FX 24.

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

26.name: Drop & replace →
26.text:
Left to right, one position at a time: the old character drops down out of its slot and the new one drops into it. Trailing dashes past the end of the text drop away last.

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx26_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Confirmed left to right (“26:A_678” mid-way).

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

27.name: Drop & replace ←
27.text:
Same as FX 26 but right to left: the rightmost dashes drop first, F arrives last.

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx27_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Confirmed right to left (“12345_DE” mid-way).

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

28.name: Drop & replace, even then odd
28.text:
Drop-and-replace in two passes, both left to right: positions 2, 4, 6, 8 (X, 2, two dashes), then 1, 3, 5, 7 (F, space, 8, last dash).

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx28_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Confirmed: even positions first (“183A5C7E”), then odd positions starting from the left.

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

29.name: Drop & replace, scrambled
29.text:
Drop-and-replace one position at a time in a fixed scrambled order: **2, 4, 7, 6, 5, 8, 3, 1** (halfway it reads “193A56_8”). FX 33 uses exactly the same order with plucks.

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_fx29_frames.png)._

30.name: Pluck & replace →
30.text:
Left to right, one position at a time: the old character lifts up out of its slot and the new one appears in its place (the opposite of the drop effects 26-29).

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx30_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Confirmed left to right (“30:AB_78” mid-way).

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

31.name: Pluck & replace ←
31.text:
Same as FX 30 but right to left: the rightmost dashes lift away first, F arrives last.

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx31_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Confirmed right to left (“1234BCDE” mid-way).

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

32.name: Pluck & replace, even then odd
32.text:
Pluck-and-replace in two passes, both left to right: X, 3, the trailing dashes, then F, the space, 2.

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx32_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Confirmed: even positions, then 1 and 3 before 5 and 7 (“32:A5C7E”), so both passes left to right.

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

33.name: Pluck & replace, scrambled
33.text:
Pluck-and-replace one position at a time in the same fixed scrambled order as FX 29: **2, 4, 7, 6, 5, 8, 3, 1** (halfway it reads “133A5_D8”).

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_fx33_frames.png)._

34.name: Column dissolve (B)
34.text:
Very like FX 35: the dashes shrink to dots, a longer blank (~1 s), then the new text builds column by column (scattered columns first; X shows only its left half and 4 only its right stroke for a moment). The column order looks irregular, so it is marked random.

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx34_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Second take looks the same as before.

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

35.name: Column dissolve
35.text:
Confirmed by a second take. The dashes quickly shrink to dots towards their centres, a short blank, then all letters build at the same time, column by column; X shows its left half first, so within each letter it looks left to right.

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx35_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Third take: each old character shrinks to its centre column (“1:1:1:1:”) before the new text builds.

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

36.name: Pixel dissolve
36.text:
Confirmed by a second take. Dashes break into dash-dot patterns, then dots, then dark (~1 s); short blank; the new text appears half-lit with dotted pixels and fills in solid. Finer and slower than FX 35.

_Proposed from camera footage PXL_20261101_224317499.mp4 (frames: captures/PXL_20261101_224317499_fx36_frames.png)._

**Third capture:** Third take: pixel dissolve again.

_Checked against PXL_20261101_225207100.mp4 with distinct characters (captures/PXL_20261101_225207100_overview_frames.png)._

37.text: Like a window shade: a wiper sweeps right to left and blanks the old text, then sweeps back left to right revealing the new text, which is already in place.
37.name: Window shade
